hypothesis.statement: The premise handed to this lane - 'count-symmetric, so the surplus mr offsets a missing add, so it is WebFrank-eligible' - has the implication backwards, and the correction generalises. Instruction-COUNT parity is necessary for postprocessor candidacy but not sufficient; the binding condition is OPCODE-MULTISET parity, because every shipped class is either a bijection on atoms (permutation) or an edit confined to register fields (recolor, copy-form), and neither can create or destroy an opcode. An `mr` that 'offsets' a missing `add` is exactly a multiset asymmetry wearing count symmetry as a disguise: the two functions' counts agree precisely BECAUSE two different opcodes cancel, which is the signature of a residual outside every class. This is the count-SYMMETRIC sibling of claim.law.DP_a-permutation-class-lead-on-a-count-asymmetric-function-is-refuted-by-its-own-signature-before-any-build.20260903.v1, and it is refutable in the same way - from the signature, before any build.
